ledger.x: c. 600 BCE: Kosala, ruled from Shravasti, stands on Awadh as one of the four powers of the north. The infobox has 'Established: c. 7th century BCE', and 'About 500 BCE, during the reign of King Prasenajit (Pasenadi)' it 'was regarded as one of the four powers of the north'; -600 is Cliopatria's start, so the year is a…

c. 600 BCE: Kaṃsa of Kosala conquers Kāśī. Kāśī infobox 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE'; 'Kāśī was finally conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kaṃsa'. The Kosala page's lead says only 'It annexed the powerful kingdom of Kashi' (no date) and its history section 'By the 5th century BCE under…

c. 451 BCE: Magadha absorbs Kosala after Ajatashatru kills Viḍūḍabha. 'it was finally defeated and absorbed into the Magadha kingdom in the 5th century BCE'; 'Viḍūḍabha was defeated and killed by the Māgadhī king Ajātasattu'; infobox 'Disestablished: c. 5th century BCE'. The page gives the century only; -451 is…

wars.name: Kosala-Magadha war over the Kāśī village
wars.outcome: Pasenadi 'revoked his rights over the village in Kāśī, after which a war between Kosala and Magadha ensued'; he then 'gave him in marriage his daughter Vajirā, to whom he gifted the village in Kāśī, and restored him to his throne.'

wars.name: Magadhan conquest of Kosala (Ajatashatru and Viḍūḍabha)
wars.outcome: 'Viḍūḍabha was defeated and killed by the Māgadhī king Ajātasattu' and Kosala was 'absorbed into the Magadha kingdom in the 5th century BCE'.

certainty.note: Only rivers bound the kingdom (Gomti, Sarpika, Sadanira) and the Nepal hills; the Kāśī frontier, the Sakya and Koliya republics and Videha are all approximate.
